Notes.Text:
This update for gnome-podcasts fixes the following issues:

Changes in gnome-podcasts:

- Update vendor dependencies (bsc#1274520 bsc#1285866 CVE-2026-25541 CVE-2026-63430)

- Migrate to xz compression and manual service run

- Update to version 0.7.1:
  + Fixed screenshot link.

- Changes from version 0.7.0:
  + Added:
    - Replace add button popover with dedicated page.
    - discovery: add a spinner on the search result subscribe
      button.
    - feed_manager: add a locked feed refresh manager
    - app: add additional keyboard shortcuts.
    - episode_description: add stream/download/play/delete buttons.
  + Changed:
    - podcasts-gtk: player: replace "mpris_player" with
      "mpris_server"
    - gtk: Create the widgets in the background before inserting
      them.
    - lazy_load: Improve the loading of widgets.
    - Use newer libadwaita 1.4 widgets.
  + Fixed:
    - data: Don't identify episodes by their title when they have a
      guid.
    - player_toolbar: request a minimum width.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Bytes is a utility library for working with bytes. From version 1.2.1 to before 1.11.1, Bytes is vulnerable to integer overflow in BytesMut::reserve. In the unique reclaim path of BytesMut::reserve, if the condition "v_capacity >= new_cap + offset" uses an unchecked addition. When new_cap + offset overflows usize in release builds, this condition may incorrectly pass, causing self.cap to be set to a value that exceeds the actual allocated capacity. Subsequent APIs such as spare_capacity_mut() then trust this corrupted cap value and may create out-of-bounds slices, leading to UB. This behavior is observable in release builds (integer overflow wraps), whereas debug builds panic due to overflow checks. This issue has been patched in version 1.11.1.

ammonia is a Rust library for repairing and securing untrusted HTML. Prior to 3.3.2, 4.0.2, and 4.1.3, applications that explicitly allow the math tag, annotation-xml, and at least one raw-text HTML element while disallowing the encoding attribute can permit mutation cross-site scripting. ammonia does not correctly implement annotation-xml's encoding-dependent MathML integration-point behavior after attribute filtering removes encoding, so the sanitizer validates a descendant under one namespace interpretation while the browser reparses the output under another. An attacker can use that namespace transition and an allowed raw-text HTML element to execute JavaScript when a user renders the sanitized output. The required tags are not enabled by default, so applications that do not explicitly allow them are not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 3.3.2, 4.0.2, and 4.1.3.
